articles.title: Designing useful empty states
articles.excerpt: Help people take the next step.
articles.body: Explain why a list is empty and offer a clear next action. A good empty state names the missing thing, shows what success looks like, and gives one button that starts that work.

articles.title: Getting started with mock data
articles.excerpt: Build interfaces before your backend is ready.
articles.body: Keep sample records consistent and include realistic variations. Shared IDs across products, carts, and orders let a prototype survive the first design review.

articles.title: A daily sketch habit
articles.excerpt: Make space for small creative experiments.
articles.body: Start with five minutes and one simple subject. The point is a mark on paper, not a finished piece you would post.

articles.title: Error copy that does not blame the user
articles.excerpt: Say what failed, why it matters, and what to try next.
articles.body: Skip 'invalid input'. Name the field, show an example that works, and keep the typed value so people are not starting over.

articles.title: Stable IDs beat pretty fixtures
articles.excerpt: Rename a title, keep the primary key.
articles.body: When a cart line item points at prod-013, that product has to exist tomorrow. Pretty names change; IDs should not.

articles.title: Shipping a quiet algorithm
articles.excerpt: The best tools disappear after they work.
articles.body: If a feature needs a tour, it is probably still noisy. Cut the chrome until someone can ignore it and still finish the job.

articles.title: One subject for a week
articles.excerpt: Draw the same mug until it stops being precious.
articles.body: Repeating a subject is faster than hunting for a new one. By Thursday the lines get honest.

articles.title: Research notes nobody files
articles.excerpt: A one-page interview recap beats a 40-slide readout.
articles.body: Write the quote, the job they were doing, and the one change you would ship. Archive the rest.

articles.title: How we edit the weekly digest
articles.excerpt: Cut first, then add one sentence of context.
articles.body: Every link needs a why. If we cannot say it in one line, it does not ship on Friday.

articles.title: Loading states that tell the truth
articles.excerpt: Skeletons are fine. Fake completed data is not.
articles.body: Show structure, not a made-up total. If the request fails, swap the skeleton for the error, not a zero.

articles.title: Tables that survive a long name
articles.excerpt: Truncate the cell, not the meaning.
articles.body: Give the primary column room, put secondary facts behind a row expand, and never wrap a status chip onto two lines.
